scope: Theorem 3.12 (Equivariant vanishing and invariant vectors) of the manuscript “The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three” (preprints/The-Kervaire-Invariant-Problem-at-the-Prime-Three-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 309 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4b9f1ff903605ffa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every integer n, including after meromorphic localization, HomC,S0 (W, Pn) = 0. Every nonzero invariant integral vector in WPn evaluates as a constant multiple of hd, where 8d = 2 − 3n, d ≥ 0. If h occurs in WP−2, the corresponding line ℓ = hP2 ⊂ W is primitive and stable. After extension to D′, its quotient has character w−15χ. More generally, if h1+3k occurs in WP−2−8k, k ≥ 0, then h already occurs in WP−2.
